name: Galibi Carib

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Galibi Carib (gali1262).

notes: Research. Cariban language (Kariña/Kali'na, a.k.a. Galibi Carib) of Venezuela and the Guianas, Latin orthography (Hoff 1968). The grapheme ï (also seen written ɨ in some sources/dictionaries, mapped equivalently) denotes the high central vowel /ɨ/. The glottal stop is written with an apostrophe, whose exact codepoint varies by source text (modifier letter apostrophe ʼ, right single quotation mark ’, or plain ASCII '); all three are mapped to /ʔ/. The voiced stops b/d/g overlap with post-nasal allophones of the voiceless stops p/t/k and are treated by some descriptions as conditioned rather than independent; they are mapped here at face value. Word stress falls on the final syllable in the disyllabic-dominant WOLD gold sample (Hoff 1968); marked here as final by default. Palatalization allophones ([tʃ ʃ ɲ]) and fricative allophones ([β]) that the spelling does not distinguish are left unencoded; there is no tone. The WOLD gold sample also contains a minority of French-loanword entries spelled in French orthography (e.g. ⟨fromage⟩, ⟨mercredi⟩) rather than adapted Kali'na spelling; these are outside this spec's Kali'na grapheme map and are not modelled. GRAVE-ACCENT VOWELS (à è ì ò ù ỳ): the Suriname/French-Guiana practical orthography codified by Courtz (2008, 'A Carib Grammar and Dictionary', §1.1 p.1, §2.5.6-2.5.8 pp.43-45) writes a coda archiphoneme /Q/ -- 'all that is left of a lost syllable po or pu' -- with a grave accent on the preceding vowel; Courtz states directly that 'the accent grave... represents a glottal stop in the pronunciation' (p.1), so grave-vowel graphemes are mapped here as vowel+/ʔ/. This matches the car wikipron gold in every non-plosive environment (before nasals, glides, liquids, vowels in hiatus, and word-finally: e.g. nàna -> a ʔ n a, wòi -> o ʔ i, kò -> k o ʔ). Courtz also documents (§2.5.8 p.44-45) that this same /Q/ surfaces as preaspiration [h], not [ʔ], specifically before a following voiceless stop /p t k/ (e.g. wàto -> w a h t o, àka -> a h k a); the wikipron gold shows this split consistently. The engine's positional-grapheme context classes (before_vowel/before_consonant, before_a/e/i/o/u, before_front/back_vowel, before/after_palatal) have no 'before a following plosive' class, so the plosive-triggered [h] allophone is left undifferentiated from the general /ʔ/ mapping -- a known, documented residual PER cost on grave-vowel+plosive words rather than a spec error. The single grapheme f is attested once in the WOLD gold sample (kofu 'fist'); Courtz's dictionary marks this entry '[Sr kofu]' (p.24255 of the extracted dictionary text), i.e. a loanword from Sranan Tongo (Surinamese Creole) -- /f/ is not part of the native Carib consonant inventory /p t k s m n r w j/ (Courtz §2.2 p.22) but is mapped here at face value since it is attested in running gold text, matching this spec's existing practice for the voiced-stop and loanword layer.

sources.notes: PhD grammar (Leiden) of Suriname/French Guiana Carib (Kari'nja), fetched in full (524 pp.). p.1: the grave accent represents a glottal stop, the residue of a lost syllable po/pu. p.22 (§2.2): the native consonant inventory is p t k s m n r w j, with no /f/. pp.43-45 (§2.5.6-2.5.8): the grave-accent orthographic vowel spells the coda archiphoneme /Q/, realised [ʔ] except before a following voiceless stop p/t/k, where it surfaces as preaspiration [h]. The dictionary body (searched via pdftotext) marks the entry kofu 'fist' as [Sr kofu], i.e. a Sranan Tongo loanword, the source of this spec's only attested /f/.
